knowledge:
- key_parameters: Sequences=A GRanges object or DNAStringSet containing the genomic regions to analyze ;; genome=A BSgenome object (e.g., Hsapiens) matching the assembly of the input sequences, required if Sequences is a GRanges object ;; pValue=P-value cutoff for declaring a binding site (default is 0.0002) ;; eValue=E-value cutoff for de novo motif discovery (default is 0.0)
- alternatives: MEME-ChIP for web-based or command-line motif discovery, Homer for motif analysis, or BCRANK for R-based heuristic motif search
- when_to_use: When analyzing high-throughput sequencing data (like ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, or DNase-seq) to identify novel DNA binding motifs and their exact binding sites within peak regions
- pitfalls: Mismatch between the genome assembly of the GRanges input and the loaded BSgenome object ;; High computational cost and memory usage when running on very large sequence sets without filtering or downsampling peaks first

workflows.name: de_novo_motif_discovery
workflows.intent: Identify novel sequence motifs from genomic peak regions using rGADEM and a reference genome.
input: peaks.bed (Genomic coordinates of ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq peaks)
workflows.stages: 1. Import peak coordinates as a GRanges object ;; 2. Load the matching BSgenome reference genome ;; 3. Run the GADEM analysis to discover motifs ;; 4. Query the resulting gadem object for identified motifs and consensus sequences
workflows.code:
library(rGADEM)
library(BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19)
# peaks is a GRanges object loaded from a BED file
gadem <- GADEM(peaks, genome = Hsapiens, verbose = 1)
nMotifs(gadem)
getConsensus(gadem)
